title: Teimuzu River Kite Flying Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ai Haibara, Ayumi, Genta, Mitsuhiko, Agasa, Officer Takagi) omitted by convention, as are pure comic-relief B-plot figures unrelated to the crime (the 'what song is Haibara humming' subplot: Higo, Sanada, Yoko Okino). No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: attempted_murder (the victim survives and regains consciousness). Old lower-fidelity file (cases/ep765-766...) named the correct culprit (Takeshi Yatsukoshi) and correct object (string telephone), so no culprit correction was needed here -- but it collapsed the case into 2 events/1 clue and was missing two plot-relevant people entirely: Takami Renno (the victim's wife, a formally-accused red herring with a solid phone alibi) and Yuitoshi Kakura's unnamed younger sister (the backstory figure whose affair with the victim and resulting suicide attempt is the motive source for BOTH red herring and true culprit). The old file's motive edge was 'unspecified (not stated in the available source excerpt)' -- the transcript actually states it plainly: Yatsukoshi had been in love with Kakura's sister since high school and resented Renno for the affair that drove her to attempt suicide. Mechanism: Yatsukoshi rigged the safety rope between two riverside kite-flying posts to leave an unmarked gap, then used a bottle-and-string telephone (disguised as him idly drinking a beverage) to feed Renno directions ('a little more to the left,' 'farther back') while both men appeared to just be flying kites; Renno, mid-phone-call with his wife and unaware he was also on the string line, backed into the gap and fell into the river. The decisive evidence was accidental: Ayumi dropped Conan's cell phone (recording app left running for an unrelated prank) near the event restroom; Yatsukoshi picked it up by mistake (same model/color as his own) and pocketed it, so it recorded his own voice -- 'Go to hell' -- as he spoke into the string phone at the moment Renno fell.

attrs.outcome: fell into the river, near-drowned, survived and regained consciousness

attrs.clearance_reason: was on a cordless landline call from home the entire time, not present at the river

persons.name: Yuitoshi Kakura
persons.occupation: alumnus, senior of the high school baseball club

attrs.clearance_reason: too far from Renno when he fell, made no gestures on the anti-cheating event video, had no phone link to him

attrs.cover_story: claimed to be too far away to have directed Renno, and that Renno had only walked to the river to dispose of a PET bottle

attrs.circumstance: had an affair with the married Ryota Renno, who promised to leave his wife for her
attrs.outcome: cut her wrist in the bathtub the night before the kite event; unconscious in serious condition in hospital

attrs.detail: posts along a riverside fence normally connected by a safety rope

attrs.mechanism: two PET bottles joined by a long taut string; Yatsukoshi spoke into his end disguised as sipping a drink, Renno unknowingly held the receiving end
attrs.signal: two tugs on the kite string prearranged as the cue to start using it

attrs.original_purpose: recording app left running to catch Ai Haibara humming
attrs.how_recovered: dropped by Ayumi near the restroom, mistakenly pocketed by Yatsukoshi (same model/color as his own)
attrs.recorded_audio: Yatsukoshi's own voice saying "Go to hell" into the string phone at the moment Renno fell

objects.name: Rigged rope at the fence posts

attrs.staging_flaw: rope from the farthest post was untied, length-matched, and retied one post over to fake an old accidental break; underside color didn't match a genuinely weathered rope, and the leftover rope segment was too long to have been the original

clues.desc: Rope-matching contradiction: reconnecting the frayed ends leaves a gap too large to bridge, one side's discoloration doesn't match sun/rain wear on the underside, and the farthest post has no rope at all -- proves the rope was deliberately moved and retied to fake a spot where a person could be led through, not an old accidental snap.

Recording comparison: the voice pattern of "Go to hell" captured on the recovered phone at the moment of the fall matches Yatsukoshi's voice, not the trash-disposal story he gave -- proving he was speaking into the string phone at that exact instant.

edges.detail: confronted Renno in person about the affair, told him to come talk after the event

edges.method: directed Renno via hidden string telephone to walk backward through the gap left by the rigged rope
